DESC	199	Establishes context on the server, which will be checked by the Broker before
DESC	199	executing any other remote procedure.  Since context is nothing more than a
DESC	199	client/server "B"-type option in the OPTION file (#19), standard MenuMan
DESC	199	security is applied in establishing a context.  Therefore, a context option
DESC	199	can be granted to user(s) exactly the same way as regular options are done
DESC	199	using MenuMan.
DESC	199	
DESC	199	A context can not be established for the following reasons:
DESC	199	
DESC	199	       · The user has no access to that option
DESC	199	
DESC	199	       · The option is temporarily out of order
DESC	199	
DESC	199	An application can switch from one context to another as often as it needs to.
DESC	199	Each time a context is created the previous context is overwritten.
DESC	199	
DESC	199	For more information on creating a context and the overall Broker security
DESC	199	see Broker on-line help documentation.

DESC	389	This Remote Procedure Call (RPC) will:

DESC	389	the Restrict Patient Record Access (#1201) field in the MAS parameters

DESC	389	security key.  If parameter set to yes and user is not a key holder , a
DESC	389	social security number must be defined in the New Person file for the user

PDESC	389	2	        0 - message will not be generated

RET	389	               Required variable not defined

RET	389	               record
RET	389	             1-Display warning message

RET	389	               or Employee and DG SECURITY OFFICER key holder

RET	389	               DG SENSITIVE RECORD BULLETIN RPC to update DG Security Log
RET	389	               file and generate Sensitive Record Access mail message.

RET	389	               Accessing own Patient file record

RET	389	warning messages will begin in RESULT(2) array.  The Privacy Act message
RET	389	is the longest message and will utilize RESULT(2)- RESULT(8).
RET	389	 
RET	389	If RESULT(1)=1, the DG Security Log file is updated.
RET	389	If RESULT(1)=2, the user must acknowledge they want to access the
RET	389	restricted record and the application must call the DG SENSITIVE RECORD
RET	389	BULLETIN RPC to update the DG Security Log file and generate the Sensitive
RET	389	Record Access mail message.

RPC	643	IBD GET ONE INPUT OBJECT	OBJLST	IBDFRPC1	2	P							1	1	RESULT,IBDF
DESC	643	This call will return specific information about any one input object
DESC	643	regardless of type.  Developers should first use the RPC to return the
DESC	643	available input objects (either by form or by clinic).  
DESC	643	 
DESC	643	There are 3 types of input objects, lists (both static and dynamic),
DESC	643	hand print fields, and multiple choice fields.  Each input object
DESC	643	may be associated with selection rules and data qualifiers.  There
DESC	643	are 4 selection rules: 
DESC	643	   0 := any number (including zero)
DESC	643	   1 := exactly one
DESC	643	   2 := at most one (0 or 1)
DESC	643	   3 := at least one (1 or more)
DESC	643	 
DESC	643	There are also a number of data qualifiers that are used to describe the
DESC	643	data, for example, primary, secondary, add to problem list, etc.
PARAM	643		IBDF	2		1
PDESC	643		The following variables are required:
PDESC	643		   IBDF("PI")     := pointer to the package interface file
PDESC	643		   IBDF("IEN")    := pointer to the input object (file depends on type)
PDESC	643		   IBDF("CLINIC") := pointer to the hospital location file (required only
PDESC	643		                     to return provider lists)
PDESC	643		   IBDF("DFN")    := pointer to patient file (required only for patient
PDESC	643		                     specific dynamic lists such as patient active problems)
PDESC	643		All are returned by one of the available rpc's in aics.
RET	643	Returns array describing input object.  See routine IBDFRPC1 for details.
RET	643	See routine IBDFDE* for examples of use.  (ibdfde2* for lists, ibdfde3 for
RET	643	hand print fields, ibdfde4 for multiple choice fields)
RET	643	 
RET	643	The return array is different for the different types of objects.

RPC	1195	ORWORB UNSIG ORDERS FOLLOWUP	ESORD	ORWORB	1								1	1	ORY,XQAID
DESC	1195	After viewing unsigned orders for a patient via an alert, evaluates
DESC	1195	whether the alert should be deleted for the current user.
DESC	1195	 
DESC	1195	The following two exception conditions exist when determining how alert
DESC	1195	deletion will occur.  In all other cases, alert deletion will occur when
DESC	1195	the patient has no unsigned orders.
DESC	1195	 
DESC	1195	1)      If the recipient of this alert does NOT have the ORES key, the
DESC	1195	alert will be deleted for that recipient after he reviews the unsigned
DESC	1195	orders. 
DESC	1195	 
DESC	1195	2)      If the recipient has the ORES key and is NOT linked to the patient
DESC	1195	as attending, inpatient primary provider or via OE/RR teams, his alert
DESC	1195	will be deleted when his unsigned orders are signed.  (If unsigned orders
DESC	1195	written by other providers for the patient remain, alerts for these other 
DESC	1195	providers will not be deleted.)  For example, a consulting surgeon (with
DESC	1195	ORES) places three unsigned orders for a patient.  He then receives an
DESC	1195	"Order requires electronic signature" alert for the patient.  He uses the 
DESC	1195	View Alerts follow-up action and is presented with ten unsigned orders for
DESC	1195	the patient.  Only three of the ten orders are his.  The surgeon signs his
DESC	1195	three unsigned orders.  If the surgeon is not linked to the patient as
DESC	1195	attending, inpatient primary providers or via OE/RR teams, the alert will 
DESC	1195	be deleted (for him only.)  
DESC	1195	 
DESC	1195	In most cases alert deletion will occur when the patient has no unsigned
DESC	1195	orders.  For example, if a recipient has the ORES key and is linked to the
DESC	1195	patient as attending, inpatient primary provider or via OE/RR teams, all
DESC	1195	unsigned orders for the patient must be signed before his alert is
DESC	1195	deleted.
PARAM	1195		XQAID	1	60	1
PDESC	1195		The alert ID.
RET	1195	Nothing returned.

RPC	1385	PSB TRANSACTION	RPC	PSBML	2	P			3				1	1	RESULTS,PSBHDR,PSBREC
DESC	1385	This is the filing RPC for all data returning from the client
DESC	1385	regarding the medication log.  Filing is handled by business rules on
DESC	1385	the server and this RPC will return either '1^Data Filed' or
DESC	1385	'-1^reason for not filing data' to the client.  Results of the 
DESC	1385	processed transaction is communicated via the RESULTS array.  The 
DESC	1385	number of RESULTS subscripts used (n) will be presented in RESULTS[0].  
DESC	1385	RESULTS [1..n] will contain the RESULTS message.  
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	Business rules are conducted via the [0] node data.  If a '+1^MEDPASS'
DESC	1385	is encountered it is a complete new med pass and is validated as such.
DESC	1385	Transaction type MEDPASS is the only type that requires a +1 in the 
DESC	1385	first piece of the header, all other transactions MUST supply a valid 
DESC	1385	medication log entry in the IENS.
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	The data for filing is passed in as a list in Param[1] as shown below.
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	Example Delphi Call
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	  with RPCBroker1 do
DESC	1385	    begin
DESC	1385	    RemoteProcedure := 'PSB TRANSACTION';
DESC	1385	    Param[0].Value := '88484^COMMENT';
DESC	1385	    Param[0].PType := Literal;
DESC	1385	    Param[1].Mult['0'] := 'Comment for the med pass';
DESC	1385	    Param[1].Ptype := List;
DESC	1385	    Call;
DESC	1385	    end;
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	-------------------------------------------------------------------------
DESC	1385	TRANSACTION = MEDPASS
DESC	1385	   Note: Entries 1-6 are required, 7,8,9 are required depending on 
DESC	1385	         item [2] order type...
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [0] = Patient IEN
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [1] = IV/Unit Dose Order Number
DESC	1385	   Note: will be passed in as I;#### for IV and U;#### for Unit Dose
DESC	1385	         future release will allow P;#### for pending
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [2] = Schedule
DESC	1385	   Note: C:Continuous P:PRN 1:One Time O:On Call
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [3] = Status
DESC	1385	   Note: G:Given H:Held R:Refused
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [4] = Orderable Item
DESC	1385	   Note: IEN to 'PHARMACY ORDERABLE ITEM' (#50.7)
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [5] = Scheduled Administration Date/Time
DESC	1385	   Note: This is when the med is scheduled, med is entered as GIVEN NOW!
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [6] = Reason Given PRN^PRN Reason Flag
DESC	1385	   Note: Required if given PRN must be null if not PRN
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [7] = Comment
DESC	1385	   Note: 1-200 characters
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [8] = Injection Site
DESC	1385	 [9] = Tab^Unique ID #
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [10..n]= RecordType^IEN^Units Ordered^Units Given^Units Type
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	          Record Type = DD:  Dispense Drug
DESC	1385	                        SOL: Solution
DESC	1385	                        ADD: Additive
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	          IEN = Internal Entry Number of the following
DESC	1385	                if Record Type = DD:  DRUG (FILE #50)  
DESC	1385	                                SOL: IV SOLUTIONS (FILE #??)
DESC	1385	                                ADD: IV ADDITIVES (FILE #??)
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	          Units Ordered = Number of units in the Inpt Meds Order
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	          Units Given = Number of units scanned/entered by the user
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	          Units Type = Type of administration unit (i.e. TAB, CAPLET, ML)
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	-------------------------------------------------------------------------
DESC	1385	TRANSACTION = COMMENT
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [0] = Comment to append to the log entry
DESC	1385	   Note: Will be appended to the log with user ien and NOW as a date
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	-------------------------------------------------------------------------
DESC	1385	TRANSACTION = PRN EFFECTIVENESS
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [0] = Effective Comment
DESC	1385	   Note: will be filed as entered now by current user
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	-------------------------------------------------------------------------
DESC	1385	TRANSACTION = STATUS UPDATE
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [0] = New Status
DESC	1385	   Note: If status is Given, Date/Time administered D/T will be set to NOW
DESC	1385	         If status is Held/Refused administered D/T will be set to null
DESC	1385	         Status on med log must be <> null to execute.
DESC	1385	         New status must NOT match current status or G will overwrite 
DESC	1385	         administration DT.
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [1] = Comment
DESC	1385	   Note: Comment *IS* Required
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	-------------------------------------------------------------------------
DESC	1385	TRANSACTION = EDIT
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [0] = Action Status
DESC	1385	 [1] = Patient DFN
DESC	1385	 [2] = Inf/Inj Site
DESC	1385	 [3] = IV Unique ID
DESC	1385	 [4] = Admin Date/Time (fileman format)
DESC	1385	 [5] = Prn Reason
DESC	1385	 [6] = Prn Effectiveness
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [7] = Comment
DESC	1385	       Note: comment data is required!
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [8] = "DD/ADD/SOL^ Drug IEN ^ Dose Ordered ^ Dose Given 
DESC	1385	         ^ Unit of Administration"
DESC	1385	 
DESC	1385	 [n] = "additional data per DD/ADD/SOL associated with order."

DESC	1513	 
DESC	1513	This remote procedure call is documented in Integration Agreement 3996.
PARAM	1513	1	GMRVDATA	1	255	1
PDESC	1513	1	This variable contains the data needed to create a Vital/Measurement
PDESC	1513	1	record in the GMRV Vital Measurement (#120.5) file. The values are parsed
PDESC	1513	1	out of the GMRVDATA variable and filed.
PDESC	1513	1	 
PDESC	1513	1	GMRVDATA has the following data:
PDESC	1513	1	 piece1^piece2^piece3^piece4^piece5
PDESC	1513	1	 
PDESC	1513	1	 where:
PDESC	1513	1	  piece1 = date/time in FileMan internal format
PDESC	1513	1	  piece2 = patient number from FILE 2 (i.e., DFN)
PDESC	1513	1	  piece3 = vital type, a semi-colon, the reading, a semi-colon, and 
PDESC	1513	1	           oxygen flow rate and percentage values [optional] (e.g.,
PDESC	1513	1	           21;99;1 l/min 90%)
PDESC	1513	1	  piece4 = hospital location (FILE 44) pointer value
PDESC	1513	1	  piece5 = user number from FILE 200 (i.e., DUZ), an asterisk, and the 
PDESC	1513	1	           qualifier (File 120.52) internal entry numbers separated by
PDESC	1513	1	           colons (e.g., 547*50:65)
RET	1513	RESULT does not return a value. 
RET	1513	 
RET	1513	The data is filed in the GMRV VITAL MEASUREMENT (#120.5) file.
RET	1513	 
RET	1513	Example:
RET	1513	 
RET	1513	 > S GMRVDATA="3051011.1635^134^1;120/80;^67^87*2:38:50:75"
RET	1513	 > D EN1^GMVDCSAV(.RESULT,GMRVDATA)

DESC	1514	This remote procedure call retrieves vital records from the GMRV Vital
DESC	1514	Measurement (#120.5) file for a selected patient within a given date span.
DESC	1514	 
DESC	1514	This remote procedure call is documented in Integration Agreement 4416.
PARAM	1514	1	GMRVDATA	1	30	1
PDESC	1514	1	GMRVDATA consists of 4 pieces of information:
PDESC	1514	1	 piece1^piece2^piece3^piece4
PDESC	1514	1

PDESC	1514	1	       piece3 = single vital type abbreviation (File 120.51, Field 1)
PDESC	1514	1	                [optional] If not defined, the default is
PDESC	1514	1	                "T;P;R;BP;HT;WT;PN;PO2;CG;CVP"
PDESC	1514	1	       piece4 = Start date of search (FileMan internal format)

RET	1514	range.

RET	1514	   SITTING, PALPATED) _VITPROVIDER,TWO
RET	1514	 
RET	1514	If there is no data, then the following is returned:
RET	1514	 
RET	1514	^TMP($J,"GRPC",1)=0^NO VITALS/MEASUREMENTS ENTERED WITHIN THIS PERIOD

RPC	1532	GMV MANAGER	RPC	GMVRPCM	4	S	0	1					1	1	RESULTS,OPTION,DATA
DESC	1532	Performs many functions for the Manager module.
DESC	1532	 
DESC	1532	This remote procedure call is documented in Integration Agreement 4360.
PARAM	1532	1	OPTION	1	10	1
PDESC	1532	1	Routine tag line in GMVRPCM to call.
PARAM	1532	2	DATA	1	100	1
PDESC	1532	2	Other data as required for the call.
RET	1532	This remote procedure call performs various actions such as building
RET	1532	selection lists and modifying package parameters. The entry point is
RET	1532	RPC^GMVRPCM. It has input parameters of RESULTS, OPTION and DATA (ex:
RET	1532	RPC^GMVRPCM(.RESULTS,OPTION,DATA). 
RET	1532

RET	1532	reference. The ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J) global array contains the results.
RET	1532

RET	1532	that will be invoked to process the call.
RET	1532

RET	1532	variable to process the call.
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	1) When the OPTION value is ADDQUAL, this RPC will link a GMRV VITAL 
RET	1532	QUALIFIER (#120.52) file entry to a GMRV VITAL TYPE (#120.51) file entry. 
RET	1532	  
RET	1532	The DATA value is a three part value separated by semi-colons(;). The 
RET	1532	first value is the FILE 120.51 internal entry number (IEN). The second 
RET	1532	value is the GMRV VITAL CATEGORY (#120.53) IEN. The third value is the 
RET	1532	GMRV VITAL QUALIFIER (#120.52).
RET	1532	  
RET	1532	Example:
RET	1532

RET	1532	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158)"
RET	1532	 > D ^%G
RET	1532	 > Global ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J
RET	1532	 > ^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158,0)=1^Qualifier Assigned
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	If an error is encountered, a "-1" followed by a caret and the error 
RET	1532	message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned. 
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	2) When the OPTION value is DELQUAL, this RPC will unlink a qualifier to 
RET	1532	a GMRV VITAL TYPE (#120.51) file entry. 
RET	1532	  
RET	1532	The DATA value is a three part value separated by semi-colons. The first 
RET	1532	value is the FILE 120.51 internal entry number (IEN). The second value is 
RET	1532	the GMRV VITAL CATEGORY (#120.53) IEN. The third value is the GMRV VITAL 
RET	1532	QUALIFIER (#120.52) IEN.
RET	1532	  
RET	1532	Example:
RET	1532	 > S DATA="1;1;1"         
RET	1532	 > S OPTION="DELQUAL"                        
RET	1532	 > D RPC^GMVRPCM(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	1532	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158)"
RET	1532	 > D ^%G
RET	1532	 > Global ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J
RET	1532	 > ^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158,0)=1^Qualifier removed.
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	If an error is encountered, a "-1" followed by a caret and the error 
RET	1532	message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned.
RET	1532

RET	1532	message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned.
RET	1532	 
RET	1532

RET	1532	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVMGR",539339804)"
RET	1532	 > D ^%G

RET	1532	 > ^TMP("GMVMGR",539339804,0)=BP
RET	1532

RET	1532	6) When the OPTION value is GETDEF, this RPC will return default template
RET	1532	names. 
RET	1532	  
RET	1532	The DATA value is a one part value. If it is null, then all default 
RET	1532	templates for that user will be returned. 
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	The TMP global contains:
RET	1532	 ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J,0)=piece1
RET	1532	 ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J,n)=piece2^piece3
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	 where piece1 = number of templates found
RET	1532	       piece2 = an IEN value, a semi-colon, and a global reference
RET	1532	       piece3 = template name
RET	1532	            n = sequential number starting with 1
RET	1532

RET	1532	 > S DATA="" 
RET	1532	 > S OPTION="GETDEF"
RET	1532	 > D RPC^GMVRPCM(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	1532	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158)"
RET	1532	 > D ^%G
RET	1532	 > Global ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J
RET	1532	 > ^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158,0)=4
RET	1532	                           1)=125;SC(^WARD 10A
RET	1532	                           2)=334;DIC(4.2,^TEST
RET	1532	                           3)=4601;VA(200,^Height ONLY
RET	1532	                           4)=547;VA(200,^All Vital Signs
RET	1532

RET	1532	values), then the default template name for that entity will be returned.

RET	1532	 ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J,0)=template name
RET	1532

RET	1532	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158)"
RET	1532	 > D ^%G

RET	1532	 > ^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158,0)=MY DEFAULT
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	If an error is encountered, a "-1" followed by a caret and the error 
RET	1532	message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned.

RET	1532	10) When the OPTION value is GETTEMP, this RPC will return a list data 
RET	1532	input templates definitions.
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	The DATA value is a two part value separated by a caret. The first part 
RET	1532	is an entity value. See IA 2263 for a list of entities. The second part is
RET	1532	a data input template name. 
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	When DATA is null, all data input template definitions are returned.
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	The TMP global contains:
RET	1532	 ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J,0)=piece1
RET	1532	 ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J,n)=piece2^piece3^piece4^piece5^piece6
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	  where piece1 = number of entries returned
RET	1532	        piece2 = 1, 2, 3, or 4. (1 = Domain, 2 = Institution, 3 = Hospital
RET	1532	                 location and 4 = New Person)
RET	1532	        piece3 = file IEN, a semi-colon and global reference
RET	1532	        piece4 = Field .01 value of the file specified in piece3
RET	1532	        piece5 = template name
RET	1532	        piece6 = template description text, a bar, vital type IEN (FILE 
RET	1532	120.51), a colon, a metric flag (0=U.S. and 1=metric), category IEN
RET	1532	(FILE 120.53), a coma, and a qualifier IEN (FILE 120.52), a tilde
RET	1532	indicates additional category and qualifier combinations for the vital
RET	1532	type. A semi-colon indicates the start of the next vital type.
RET	1532	             n = sequential number starting with 1
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	Example:
RET	1532	 > S DATA="USR",OPTION="GETTEMP"               
RET	1532	 > D RPC^GMVRPCM(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	1532	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158)"
RET	1532	 > D ^%G
RET	1532	 > Global ^TMP("GMVMGR",$J
RET	1532	 > ^TMP("GMVMGR",539356158,0)=1
RET	1532	                           1)=4^547;VA(200,^VITUSER,ONE^MY DEFAULT^ALL
RET	1532	                              VITALS|1:0:1,2~2,59~3,50;20:1
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	 
RET	1532	If an error is encountered, a "-1" followed by a caret and the error 
RET	1532	message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned.
RET	1532

RPC	1533	GMV WARD/ROOM PATIENTS	ROOMPT	GMVUTL7	2	R	0						1	1	RESULTS,GMVWRD,GMVRLST
DESC	1533	Returns a list of patients in the ward and rooms specified.
PARAM	1533	1	GMVWRD	1	60	1
PDESC	1533	1	Name of the ward (e.g., 2EAST).
PARAM	1533	2	GMVRLST	1	150	1
PDESC	1533	2	The room numbers of the ward separated by comma (e.g., 200,210,220).
RET	1533	RESULT(n)=patient name^DFN^DOB (external)^SSN (no hyphens)
RET	1533	 where n is a sequential number beginning with 0 (zero)
RPC	1534	GMV GET CURRENT TIME	TIME	GMVUTL7	1	S	0	0					1	1	RESULT,P2
DESC	1534	Gets the current date and time from the server.
DESC	1534	 
DESC	1534	This remote procedure call is documented in Integration Agreement 4355.
RET	1534	Returns current date and time in FileMan internal and external format.
RET	1534	 
RET	1534	Example:

RPC	1535	GMV USER	RPC	GMVRPCU	4	S	0	1					1	1	RESULTS,OPTION,DATA
DESC	1535	Retrieves data about the user (e.g., parameter settings).
DESC	1535	 
DESC	1535	This remote procedure call is documented in Integration Agreement 4366.
PARAM	1535	1	OPTION	1	10	1
PDESC	1535	1	Routine tag line to call in GMVRPCU.
PARAM	1535	2	DATA	1	100	1
PDESC	1535	2	Other data as required for the call.
RET	1535	This Remote Procedure Call (RPC) performs various actions focusing on the 
RET	1535	user. The entry point is RPC^GMVRPCU. It has input parameters of RESULTS, 
RET	1535	OPTION and DATA (e.g., RPC^GMVRPCU(RESULTS,OPTION,DATA)). 
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The RESULTS variable contains the results of the call or the location 
RET	1535	where the results can be found.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The OPTION variable identifies another entry point in the GMVRPCU routine 
RET	1535	that is invoked to process the call.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The DATA variable contains any values needed by the OPTION variable to 
RET	1535	process the call.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	1) When the OPTION value is SETPAR, this RPC will set and/or delete the 
RET	1535	value of a GMV USER DEFAULTS setting (e.g., the user's default template).
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The DATA value is a two part value separated by a caret. The first part  
RET	1535	is name of a setting. The second part is the value of the setting. If the 
RET	1535	second part is null, the existing value of the setting is deleted.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The TMP global contains:
RET	1535	 ^TMP("GMVUSER",$J,0)=1^Parameter set.
RET	1535	 or
RET	1535	 ^TMP("GMVUSER",$J,0)=1^Parameter cleared
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	Example:
RET	1535	 > S DATA="DefaultTemplate^547;VA(200,|MY DEFAULT",OPTION="SETPAR"
RET	1535	 > D RPC^GMVRPCU(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	1535	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVUSER",539374023)"
RET	1535	 > D ^%G
RET	1535	 > Global ^TMP("GMVUSER",$J
RET	1535	 > ^TMP("GMVUSER",539374023,0)=1^Parameter set.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	If an error is encountered, a "-1" followed by a caret and the error 
RET	1535	message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	2) When the OPTION value is GETPAR, this RPC will return the value of the
RET	1535	GMV USER DEFAULTS setting specified in the DATA value.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The DATA value is a one part value. It is the name of a setting (e.g., 
RET	1535	the user's default template).
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	 The TMP global contains:
RET	1535	  ^TMP("GMVUSER",$J,0)=value of setting or null
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	Example:
RET	1535	 > S DATA="DefaultTemplate",OPTION="GETPAR"       
RET	1535	 > D RPC^GMVRPCU(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	1535	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVUSER",539374023)"
RET	1535	 > D ^%G
RET	1535	 > Global ^TMP("GMVUSER",$J
RET	1535	 > ^TMP("GMVUSER",539374023,0)=547;VA(200,|ONE VITAL TYPE ONLY
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	3) When the OPTION value is SIGNON, this RPC will return information about
RET	1535	the user who is currently signed onto the system.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The DATA value is not used. The user's IEN (i.e., DUZ) to the NEW PERSON 
RET	1535	(#200) file value must be defined when this call is made.
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	The RESULT variable will return the following array:
RET	1535	  RESULT(0)=NEW PERSON (#200) file internal entry number (DUZ)
RET	1535	  RESULT(1)=User's name (FILE 200, Field .01)
RET	1535	  RESULT(2)=Domain (FILE 4.2) internal entry number
RET	1535	  RESULT(3)=Domain name (FILE 4.2, Field .01)
RET	1535	  RESULT(4)=Institution (FILE 4) internal entry number the user is signed
RET	1535	             into (i.e., DUZ(2))
RET	1535	  RESULT(5)=Institution name (FILE 4, Field .01)
RET	1535	  RESULT(6)="0" or "1". "1" indicates the user has the GMV MANAGER or 
RET	1535	             programmer key. "0" indicates the user has neither key.
RET	1535	  RESULT(7)=The user's title (FILE 200, Field 8)
RET	1535	  RESULT(8)=This value is always null.
RET	1535	  RESULT(9)=Number of seconds the system will wait for a response from 
RET	1535	             the user (i.e., DTIME). The default time is 300 seconds.
RET	1535	  RESULT(10)=INSTITUTION (#4) file IEN^FILE 4 external value^station 
RET	1535	              number (e.g., 499^SUPPORT ISC^499).
RET	1535	 
RET	1535	Example:
RET	1535	 > S OPTION="SIGNON"
RET	1535	 > D RPC(.RESULT,OPTION) ZW RESULT
RET	1535	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVUSER",539375907)"
RET	1535	 > D ^%G
RET	1535	 > Global ^TMP("GMVUSER",$J
RET	1535	 > ^TMP("GMVUSER",539375907,0)=547
RET	1535	                            1)=VITUSER,ONE
RET	1535	                            2)=334
RET	1535	                            3)=DEV.DEV.FO-HINES.MED.VA.GOV
RET	1535	                            4)=499
RET	1535	                            5)=SUPPORT ISC
RET	1535	                            6)=1
RET	1535	                            7)=PROGRAMMER
RET	1535	                            8)=
RET	1535	                            9)=9999
RET	1535	                           10)=499^SUPPORT ISC^499

DESC	2036	BCMA Medication Log Look Up Remote Procedures.
DESC	2036	 
DESC	2036	This routine is a conglomerate of  Medication Log lookup functionality
DESC	2036	per the BCMA Graphical User Interface software.
DESC	2036

DESC	2036	                       value of selected item. (PSB IEN per SELECTAD)
DESC	2036	               (2)     search date per ADMLKUP
DESC	2036	    
DESC	2036	Output: RESULTS (array)
DESC	2036	        RESULTS(0)    number of lookup matches
DESC	2036	               (1)    error message or data per match/selection
DESC	2036	               (n)    data per subsequent match/selection.

DESC	2036	piece 7         ""
DESC	2036	piece 8         ""
DESC	2036	piece 9         ""

DESC	2036	piece 11        Social Security Number (displayable format)
DESC	2036	 
DESC	2036	 
DESC	2036

DESC	2036	piece 10        PRN Effectiveness
DESC	2036	 
DESC	2036	 
DESC	2036

DESC	2036

DESC	2036

DESC	2036	piece 12        "for possible later use"

DESC	2036

PDESC	4141	2	 ;               comment is free-text

RET	4141	 ;     ERROR_ID^MESSAGE
RET	4141	 ;        2=general error
RET	4141	 ;    Accession related errors return an entry for each lab pointer
RET	4141	 ;    that is passed in:
RET	4141	 ;     ERROR_ID^MESSAGE

RPC	4158	GMV LOCATION SELECT	RPC	GMVRPCHL	4	S	0	1					1	1	RESULTS,OPTION,DATA
DESC	4158	Select a hospital location by name, from a patient appointment or from a
DESC	4158	patient admission.
DESC	4158	 
DESC	4158	This remote procedure is documented in Integration Agreement 4461.
PARAM	4158	1	OPTION	1	10	1
PDESC	4158	1	Routine tag line in GMVRPCHL to call.
PARAM	4158	2	DATA	1	100	1
PDESC	4158	2	Other data as required for the call.
RET	4158	This remote procedure call allows the user to select a hospital location. 
RET	4158	The entry point is RPC^GMVRPCHL. It has input parameters of RESULTS, 
RET	4158	OPTION and DATA (ex. RPC^GMVRPCHL(.RESULTS,OPTION,DATA).
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	The RESULTS variable will contain the ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J) global array 
RET	4158	reference. The ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J) global array contains the results.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	The OPTION variable identifies a line label in the GMVRPCHL routine that 
RET	4158	will be invoked to process the call.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	The DATA variable contains any additional values needed by the OPTION 
RET	4158	variable to process the call.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 1) When the OPTION value is NAME, this RPC will do a file lookup.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The DATA value is a three part value separated by carets(^). The first 
RET	4158	 part is a file number. The second part is a value to look up. The third
RET	4158	 part is the field or fields to do the look up on. If the third piece is
RET	4158	 not defined, the lookup is done on the .01 field of the file.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The TMP global contains:
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,0)=piece1
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,n)=piece2^piece3
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	   where piece1 = number of entries found
RET	4158	         piece2 = file number, a semi-colon and record IEN
RET	4158	         piece3 = field value
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 Example:
RET	4158	 >S OPTION="NAME",DATA="44^OUTPATIENT^.01"    
RET	4158	 >D RPC^GMVRPCHL(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	4158	 >RESULT="^TMP("GMVHLOC",539052767)"
RET	4158	 >D ^%G
RET	4158	 >Global ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J
RET	4158	 >^TMP("GMVHLOC",539052767,0)=3
RET	4158	                          1)=44;75^OUTPATIENT NUC MED
RET	4158	                          2)=44;74^OUTPATIENT RADIOLOGY
RET	4158	                          3)=44;80^OUTPATIENT ULTRASOUND
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 2) When the OPTION value is APPT, this RPC will return a list of clinic 
RET	4158	 appointments for the patient.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The DATA value is a four part value separated by carets(^). The first 
RET	4158	 piece is DFN. The second piece is the start date of the search. If 
RET	4158	 not defined, this value defaults to 365 days prior to today. The third 
RET	4158	 piece is the end date of the search. If not defined, the value defaults 
RET	4158	 to today. Both dates are in FileMan internal format. The fourth piece is
RET	4158	 a string of numbers to indicate what types of appointments to return. If
RET	4158	 not defined, the value defaults to "123456789" (i.e., all appointment
RET	4158	 types) where:
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 1 - Active/Kept
RET	4158	 2 - Inpatient appts. only
RET	4158	 3 - No-shows 
RET	4158	 4 - No-shows, auto-rebook
RET	4158	 5 - Cancelled by clinic
RET	4158	 6 - Cancelled by clinic, auto rebook
RET	4158	 7 - Cancelled by patient
RET	4158	 8 - Cancelled by patient, auto rebook
RET	4158	 9 - No action taken
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The TMP global contains:
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,0)=piece1
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,n)=piece2^piece3^piece4^piece5^piece6^piece7
RET	4158	                       ^piece8^piece9^
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	   where piece1 = number of entries found
RET	4158	         piece2 = date/time of appt (FM internal)
RET	4158	         piece3 = date/time of appt (external)
RET	4158	         piece4 = hospital location IEN (FILE 44)
RET	4158	         piece5 = hospital location name (FILE 44, Field .01)
RET	4158	         piece6 = appt status (internal)
RET	4158	         piece7 = appt status (external)
RET	4158	         piece8 = appt type (internal)
RET	4158	         piece9 = appt type (external)
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 Example:
RET	4158	 > S OPTION="APPT",DATA="78^3051201^3051206^"   
RET	4158	 > D RPC^GMVRPCHL(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	4158	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVHLOC",539052767)"
RET	4158	 > D ^%G
RET	4158	 > Global ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J
RET	4158	 > ^TMP("GMVHLOC",539052767,0)=1
RET	4158	                            1)=3051206.1^DEC 6,2005@10:00^88^WEIGHT 
RET	4158	                               CLINIC^^^9^REGULAR
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 3) When the OPTION value is ADMIT, this RPC will return a list of 
RET	4158	 hospital admissions for the patient specified.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The DATA value is the patient's DFN.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The TMP global contains:
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,0)=piece1
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,n)=piece2^piece3^piece4^piece5^piece6
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	   where piece1 = number of entries found
RET	4158	         piece2 = date/time of admission (external) 
RET	4158	         piece3 = hospital location IEN (FILE 44)
RET	4158	         piece4 = hospital location name (FILE 44, Field .01)
RET	4158	         piece5 = type of movement (FILE 405.1, Field .01)
RET	4158	         piece6 = movement IEN (FILE 405)
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 Example:
RET	4158	 > S OPTION="ADMIT",DATA=134
RET	4158	 > D RPC^GMVRPCHL(.RESULT,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULT
RET	4158	 > RESULT="^TMP("GMVHLOC",539052767)"
RET	4158	 > D ^%G
RET	4158	 > Global ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J
RET	4158	 > ^TMP("GMVHLOC",539052767,0)=1 
RET	4158	                            1)=Apr 09, 2001 1:48:43 pm^67^
RET	4158	                               2-ASM^DIRECT^1712 
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	If an error is encountered for NAME, ADMIT or APPT, a "-1" followed by a
RET	4158	caret and the error message text (i.e., -1^error message) is returned in 
RET	4158	RESULT(0).
RET	4158	 The DATA value is FROM^MAXIMUM^DIRECTION.
RET	4158	    Where:
RET	4158	          FROM = Value to begin the search (optional). Default is 
RET	4158	                 null (i.e., start with the first entry in the B x-ref).
RET	4158	       MAXIMUM = Maximum number of entries to return. (optional) 
RET	4158	                 Default is 100.
RET	4158	     DIRECTION = Direction of search (optional). 1 means forward and -1 
RET	4158	                 means backwards. Default is 1.
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	 The TMP global contains:
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,0)=piece1
RET	4158	  ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J,n)=piece2^piece3
RET	4158	            
RET	4158	   where piece1 = number of entries found
RET	4158	         piece2 = 44;ien (44, a semi-colon and the entry number)
RET	4158	         piece3 = location name (FILE 44, Field .01)
RET	4158	         n is a sequential number starting with zero
RET	4158	                  
RET	4158	 Example:
RET	4158	 > S OPTION="CLINIC",DATA="A^5^1"                           
RET	4158	 > K RESULTS D RPC^GMVRPCHL(.RESULTS,OPTION,DATA) ZW RESULTS
RET	4158	 > RESULTS="^TMP("GMVHLOC",540221719)"
RET	4158	 > D ^%G
RET	4158	 > Global ^TMP("GMVHLOC",$J
RET	4158	 > ^TMP("GMVHLOC",540221719,0)=5
RET	4158	                            1)=44;140^ANDY'S AUDIO NON-COUNT CLINIC
RET	4158	                            2)=44;139^ANDY'S AUDIOLOGY COUNT CLINIC
RET	4158	                            3)=44;76^AUDIOLOGY AND SPEECH PATHOLOGY
RET	4158	                            4)=44;87^BARB'S CLINIC
RET	4158	                            5)=44;217^BOISE OUTPATIENT
RET	4158	 
RET	4158	If an error is encountered for NAME, ADMIT, APPT or CLINIC, a "-1"
RET	4158	followed by a caret and the error message text (i.e., -1^error message) is
RET	4158	returned in RESULT(0).
